name: Breck Baobab-Tamarind Cola
description: A dark, cola-adjacent carbonated drink that replaces the traditional cola flavor profile with a West African-inspired blend of synth-baobab and real tamarind concentrate, giving it a distinctive tart-sweet depth that loyal drinkers prefer to conventional cola.
flavor_profile: Dark, tangy, and complex — caramel-adjacent sweetness from baobab, sharp tamarind tartness, faint woody undertone, cola-like carbonation punch but with more flavor dimension than traditional cola
cultural_context: Breck Baobab-Tamarind has been trying for two decades to unseat the top-tier colas and has never quite managed it, but it has an intensely loyal Tier 1-2 following that views it as a point of pride over the 'bland' market leaders. It's the classic underdog brand — always the 'actually better' choice in taste tests among its fans, always outspent in marketing by its competitors.
story_hooks: Breck's formula for the tamarind-baobab blend was allegedly stolen from a smaller street brand fifteen years ago — the original creator, now elderly and living in the Shelf, has a grandchild who just found the original recipe documentation and wants to do something with it.

Breck is about to be acquired by one of the top-five corponation beverage giants, who plan to 'streamline' the recipe to cut costs — the acquisition is not yet public, and the Breck employees who know are trying to decide what to do.

A Shelf community has organized an informal 'Breck economy' where the cans serve as a stable barter unit — Breck corporate has just discovered this and is deeply uncertain whether to be flattered, concerned, or both.
